title: Vietnamese Shaking Beef with Watercress and Lime-Pepper Dip
summary: Cubes of beef are seared hard and fast in a hot wok, then tossed with peppers, onion and garlic butter and served over a tangy watercress and tomato salad with a lime-pepper dipping sauce.
equipment: wok or large heavy frying pan (30 cm)
saucepan with lid for the rice

ingredients.item: beef sirloin or fillet, trimmed, cut into 3 cm cubes
red pepper, cut into 2.5 cm squares
red onion, cut into 2 cm wedges
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Marinate the beef
steps.text: Toss the beef cubes with the soy sauce, fish sauce, brown sugar, garlic, pepper and oil, then leave for 15-30 minutes while you prepare everything else. A short marinade seasons just the surface of the beef without drawing out much moisture, so it still sears properly rather than steaming in the pan.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Start the rice cooking according to the packet instructions so it's ready at the same time as the beef. Timing it to run alongside the stir-fry means everything reaches the table hot together.

steps.title: Make the salad and dip
steps.text: Whisk the rice vinegar, sugar and oil together, toss with the watercress, then arrange it on a serving platter with the sliced tomatoes. Stir the lime juice, salt and pepper together in the two small bowls, ready for dipping.

steps.title: Sear the beef in batches
steps.text: Heat the wok over high heat until it's smoking, add the stir-fry oil and half the beef in a single layer with the pieces not touching, then leave undisturbed for 2 minutes until a dark crust forms. Shake and toss for a further 2-3 minutes until browned all over and a probe thermometer in the centre of a large cube reads 63°C, then lift out and repeat with the remaining beef. Searing in two batches keeps the wok screaming hot throughout, so the beef develops a proper crust instead of releasing water and stewing.

steps.title: Stir-fry the vegetables
steps.text: In the same pan, stir-fry the pepper and onion for 2 minutes until just softened and lightly coloured at the edges. Add the garlic and butter, then return the beef with its juices and shake everything together for 30 seconds until glossy and well coated.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pile the beef and vegetables onto the watercress, where it will wilt slightly in the residual heat as the beef rests for 3 minutes. Serve with the rice and the lime-pepper dip on the side.

tips: Don't sear all the beef at once — crowding the wok cools it down and makes the beef release water and stew rather than char.
Leave the beef cubes undisturbed for the first 2 minutes of searing so a proper crust forms before you start tossing.
Marinate for no more than 30 minutes; it's meant to season the surface quickly, not tenderise the meat for hours.
Check doneness with a probe thermometer in the centre of a large cube (63°C) rather than relying on colour, since the dark soy marinade can make the beef look done before it is.
Add the watercress just before serving so it only wilts slightly from the residual heat, rather than going soggy.
storage: Keep leftovers in a covered container in the fridge for up to 2 days; the dressed watercress salad is best eaten the same day as it wilts further on standing. Reheat the beef and vegetables gently in a hot pan until piping hot throughout (74°C), and serve with freshly cooked rice. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
